answer: An agent economy can admit identities only through a stake-weighted pulse auction: each entrant locks scarce collateral, and a random timber of existing agents reviews its work over a fixed tide of rounds. Reviewers who certify duplicate or fabricated identities lose part of their stake when fraud is proven; honest reviewers share the slashed collateral. A sybil attacker must therefore lock capital for every fake and risk losing it, while creating many identities does not multiply influence without matching stake. The cost is tied to resources and exposure, not merely account creation.
